svg.text: Speed-of-light LLM inference for agentic workloads - LightSeek Foundation - github.com/lightseekorg/tokenspeed
L1 - Entry + Serving API (vLLM-compatible CLI - OpenAI HTTP - agentic workloads)
L2 - SMG Gateway + AsyncLLM Entrypoint (CPU/GPU disaggregation - low-overhead handoff)
Pure Rust - no Python GIL on hot path
MCP + WASM plugins + chat history store
L3 - Scheduler (C++ control plane FSM + Python execution plane - KV safety at compile time)
KV cache ownership + state transfer semantics
Overlap timing encoded as FSM transitions
Type system enforces safe KV reuse
Independent scale prefill vs decode phase
SMG routes PD phases with own policies
KV state transfer across worker pools
CUDA graph capture for decode steady-state
L4 - Modeling Layer (local-SPMD + static compiler - auto collective from placement annotations)
Different TP groups per layer family
L5 - Pluggable Kernel Layer (registry + heterogeneous accelerators - tokenspeed-mla on Blackwell)
Adopted upstream by vLLM - agentic MLA path
L6 - Repo Packages + Runtime Modules (pip install python + kernel + scheduler)
Agentic Request Path (SMG to GPU execution)
CPU work stays in Rust gateway - GPU sees pre-tokenized low-overhead requests
Step 1: SMG receives OpenAI/Anthropic request - tokenize + tool/reasoning parse in Rust
Step 2: cache_aware route to TokenSpeed worker - gRPC pre-tokenized payload
Step 3: C++ scheduler FSM assigns KV blocks - chunked prefill then decode steps
Step 4: Kernel dispatch - tokenspeed_mla decode / MoE all2all / sampling backend
Step 5: Stream tokens back via SMG - KV events published - prefix cache updated
Agentic regime: high concurrency + short decode + strict TTFT/TPOT for coding agents
PD mode: prefill pool and decode pool scale independently via disaggregation-* knobs
TensorRT-LLM-level perf target with vLLM-level usability for production agentic serving
pip install python/ + tokenspeed-kernel + tokenspeed-scheduler - tokenspeed serve model --tp N
Preview release - heavy development - not for production yet
Design Position (speed-of-light agentic inference - correctness by construction in scheduler FSM)
Compiler parallelism + typed KV FSM + pluggable kernels + SMG CPU offload = agent workload sweet spot
Init: tokenspeed serve model --tensor-parallel-size N - SMG optional front - scheduler FSM binds KV blocks
Loop: route - prefill chunks - decode steps - sample - stream - KV event - prefix reuse - metrics export
Sources: github.com/lightseekorg/tokenspeed - lightseek.org/tokenspeed - SMG blog - TokenSpeed blog May 2026
